message.content:
Carabiners for climbing are generally classified as snap hooks of base metal. Heading 7326 covers other articles of iron or steel, and heading 8308 covers clasps, frames with clasps, buckles, and hooks of base metal for clothing, footwear, awnings, handbags, travel goods, or other made-up articles. CBP rulings on climbing carabiners have classified them in 7326.19 (forged articles of iron or steel) or 7326.90. Since these are hot-forged steel with an aluminum gate, the forged-steel route seems most likely.

I recall that the Alpha Steel ruling, probably for Black Diamond or a similar brand, classified it in 7326.19.0010. Under HTSUS 7326.19, "Other, forged or otherwise worked by hammering" has 7326.19.0010 for "Articles of iron or steel, forged" and 7326.19.0080 for others. I recall that "7326.19.0010" is the code for "Other, forged: Other". Other rulings classify aluminum carabiners in 7616.99.

However, some rulings placed carabiners in 8308.90 as clasps and snap hooks, and the forged carabiner code in 7326.19.00 is a plausible alternative. I'll go with 7326.19.0010.

{"hts_code": "7326.19.0010", "reason": "The carabiners are hot-forged carbon steel articles, so they fall under other forged articles of iron or steel in heading 7326, with the aluminum gate and other parts being minor components."}
